body.statement: For \(p\geq3\), fixed \(\iota\), and finite \(\Xi\), the procedure terminates after at most \(G_{\#}2^{c_{\max}}+G_{\#}2^{b_{\max}}+(G_{\#}+\binom{G_{\#}}{2})4^{b_{\max}}\) chart or objective leaves and \(\mathfrak B(\Xi)\) outward-rounded operations. It rejects \(\rho\notin\Delta_J^{\mathbb Q}\) before covariance or required-well evaluation. A \(\mathtt{CERTIFIED}\) output proves full rank; normalized allocation with \(\rho_j>0\) for every composition row entering the unpooling map; valid chart coverage; positive exact untruncated bounds \(\Gamma_{\mathcal T}\geq\underline\Gamma_{\mathcal T}\), \(\kappa_{\mathcal T}\geq\underline\kappa_{\mathcal T}\), \(\Lambda_{\mathcal T}(r_{\mathrm{id}})\geq\underline\Lambda_{\mathcal T}(r_{\mathrm{id}})\), and \(\mu_{\mathcal T}(r_{\mathrm{id}};\mathscr C)\geq\underline\mu_{\mathcal T}(r_{\mathrm{id}};\mathscr C)\); positive interiority; the recorded tail and variance bounds; and \(N_{\mathrm{req}}\leq N_{\max}\). For an empty wrong-graph comparison or remote-pair set, the corresponding exact and certified bounds are \(+\infty\) and impose no numerical check. A \(\mathtt{REFUTED}\) output proves its named obstruction; \(\mathtt{UNDECIDED}\) makes no substantive claim.
body.justification: This theorem proves unconditional finite termination and one-sided soundness of every certified or refuted output. The separate \(\mathrm{thm{:}relative\text{-}eventual\text{-}certification}\) supplies the only completeness statement, under explicit strict slack and convergent controls.
body.gap: Existing validated-numerics results do not jointly propagate Poisson-PGF tails through wrong-graph, remote-subset, local-chart, covariance, and causal-precision tasks, and fixed finite controls need not decide them.
body.consumer: It turns a declared prospective design into an auditable go, stop, or undecided result, while the relative companion theorem states exactly when refinement eventually yields go.
body.proof_tex:
Every loop in \(\mathfrak C\) ranges over a finite graph set, a finite retained state set, finite multi-index and precision lists, and binary trees of prescribed depth.  A binary tree of depth \(d\) has at most \(2^d\) leaves; the stated product-box bound \(4^{b_{\max}}\) is a valid coarse ceiling.  Summing the chart, single-graph objective, same-graph remote-product, and unordered wrong-graph product trees gives at most
\[
 G_{\#}2^{c_{\max}}+G_{\#}2^{b_{\max}}
 +\left(G_{\#}+\binom{G_{\#}}2\right)4^{b_{\max}}. \tag{21}
\]
There are
\[
 P_{\mathrm{ar}}=1+
 \left\lceil\frac{b_{\mathrm{cap}}-b_0}{\Delta b}\right\rceil
\]
precision passes.  The literal recurrence and linear-algebra counts in \(\mathrm{def{:}arithmetic\text{-}complexity}\), multiplied by its leaf count including the terminal task, are exactly \(\mathfrak B(\Xi)\).  This proves unconditional finite termination and both displayed ceilings.

We next prove enclosure validity.  For a conditional Poisson variable,
\[
 \mathbb E[V_s^m\mid V_{\operatorname{pa}(s)}]
 =\sum_{k=0}^{m}
 \left\{\begin{matrix}m\\k\end{matrix}\right\}\lambda_s^k.
\]
For \(h_s=1+|\operatorname{pa}(s)|\), convexity of \(x\mapsto x^k\) on \([0,\infty)\) gives
\[
 \left(\alpha_s+\sum_u b_{su}V_u^{q_{su}}\right)^k
 \leq h_s^{k-1}
 \left(\alpha_s^k+
 \sum_u b_{su}^kV_u^{q_{su}k}\right). \tag{22}
\]
Topological induction proves that each recursive \(U_{\boldsymbol d rs}(m)\) majorizes the corresponding raw moment.  Deleting the intervened kernel and substituting a fixed count leaves the same induction valid.

Direct differentiation of a Poisson log mass, using the strictly positive lower rate \(\lambda^-_{rs}\), bounds its first derivative by \(L_{e_t}\) and every higher derivative by the displayed \(L_\nu\).  The multivariate product rule and the complete-Bell recurrence then prove inductively that
\[
 |\partial^\nu p_\theta(v)|\leq p_\theta(v)D_\nu(v). \tag{23}
\]
For \(T_R=\{v:\text{some }v_s>R_s\}\), the union bound and
\(\mathbf1\{v_s>R_s\}\leq v_s^{s_{\mathrm{tail}}}/(R_s+1)^{s_{\mathrm{tail}}}\) give
\[
 \sum_{v\in T_R}|\partial^\nu p_\theta(v)|
 \leq\sum_s
 \frac{\mathcal U_{\boldsymbol d r}(D_\nu V_s^{s_{\mathrm{tail}}})}
 {(R_s+1)^{s_{\mathrm{tail}}}}
 =E_{\boldsymbol d r,\nu}. \tag{24}
\]
Multiplication by \(V_{i_Y}+V_{i_Z}\) gives the stated intervention-and-contrast tail bound.  If \(a,b\in[0,1]\) and \(|a-\widetilde a|,|b-\widetilde b|\leq\varepsilon_0\), then
\[
 |ab-\widetilde a\widetilde b|
 \leq |a|\,|b-\widetilde b|+|\widetilde b|\,|a-\widetilde a|
 \leq2\varepsilon_0+\varepsilon_0^2, \tag{25}
\]
which validates the covariance-product enlargement.

Taylor's theorem gives, for \(x\geq0\),
\[
 \left|e^{-x}-\sum_{k=0}^{a}\frac{(-x)^k}{k!}\right|
 \leq\frac{x^{a+1}}{(a+1)!}. \tag{26}
\]
Thus the initial exponential interval is valid.  Induction through the Poisson, complete-Bell, multivariate Leibniz, and fixed Taylor recurrences preserves inclusion.  Equation (24) enlarges retained sums to cover the exact infinite sums.  Downward rounding of lower endpoints and upward rounding of upper endpoints preserve inclusion under each rational arithmetic operation; division is used only after its divisor interval excludes zero.  Consequently every recorded interval contains its exact untruncated target.

A positive lower endpoint for a wrong-graph objective therefore bounds the objective on its whole leaf.  For a remote-product leaf, the corrected rule also passes whenever the moment-distance lower endpoint is positive on the whole product box, whether or not the distance-constraint interval has a nonnegative lower endpoint.  Such positivity necessarily holds on the leaf's remote feasible subset.  Conversely, a leaf whose distance-constraint upper endpoint is negative contains no remote feasible point and is soundly discarded.  Passing leaves and discarded infeasible leaves cover the required product domain, so
\[
 \Gamma_{\mathcal T}\geq\underline\Gamma_{\mathcal T},
 \qquad
 \Lambda_{\mathcal T}(r_{\mathrm{id}})
 \geq\underline\Lambda_{\mathcal T}(r_{\mathrm{id}}). \tag{27}
\]
The interval \(LDL^{\mathsf T}\) tests respectively certify
\(J^{\mathsf T}J-u^2I\succ0\) and
\((PJ+J^{\mathsf T}P^{\mathsf T})/2-uI\succ0\) throughout their boxes.  Chart coverage then gives
\[
 \kappa_{\mathcal T}\geq\underline\kappa_{\mathcal T}>0,
 \qquad
 \mu_{\mathcal T}(r_{\mathrm{id}};\mathscr C)
 \geq\underline\mu_{\mathcal T}(r_{\mathrm{id}};\mathscr C)>0. \tag{28}
\]
Exact rational comparisons certify syntax, box validity, full rank, normalized positive row allocation, and positive inference-box clearance.  The covariance and sandwich enclosures, protected by nonzero denominator and positive-definiteness tests, give the recorded variance upper bounds.  Outward evaluation of the displayed formulas then proves \(N_{\mathrm{req}}\leq N_{\max}\).  Because the simplex check precedes all covariance and well calculations, a failed simplex is rejected at the stated stage.

For a collision test, the frozen \(\mathrm{lem{:}krawczyk\text{-}inclusion}\) gives a zero \(y\in X\) of the selected square projection.  The mean-value matrix between the center and \(y\) belongs to the Jacobian enclosure, so substituting \(F(y)=0\) in the Krawczyk expression shows \(y\in K(x,X)\).  Every omitted moment coordinate is enclosed by the singleton \([0,0]\) on that set, hence also vanishes at \(y\).  The full moment difference is zero, and the disjoint parameter factors give the recorded wrong-graph collision.  Exact rank defect, invalid boxes, and simplex failure are direct obstructions.  Thus every \(\mathtt{REFUTED}\) output proves its named obstruction.  An exhausted or failed test is assigned \(\mathtt{UNDECIDED}\), to which the definition attaches no substantive conclusion.  Empty comparison sets have their declared \(+\infty\) values and require no numerical test.  This proves every unconditional soundness assertion.
